message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on an H-Mod CEP Kit. The kit is a wiring assembly with a PCB, and it amplifies the signal. Candidate headings:

- 8518.40 (audio-frequency electric amplifiers) is a possibility.
- 8518.90 covers parts of headphones and similar goods.
- 8544.42 covers insulated wire with connectors.
- 8543.90 covers parts of electrical machines.

The kit includes a PCB with an amplifier and an impedance-matching network, and it is used in headsets. Headsets fall under 8518.30, so parts of them go under 8518.90. I recall the ruling classifying it in 8518.90.8000, "Parts: other," or possibly 8518.40.2000. Since the kit is a part of an aviation headset, it is a part of headphones, and 8518.90.80 is the best fit. The statistical suffix is 8518.90.8040 or 8518.90.8000, and I will go with 8518.90.8000.
